meta.objective: Phase 2, ARC White-Box Estimation Challenge 2026: final-layer error and metered computation on 1024-wide, 16-layer ReLU networks.

components.title: Moment propagation
components.what: Per-unit means and variances propagated layer by layer through the ReLU (the Gaussian moment closure); scale modes, centers, rms normalisation.

components.title: Covariance structure
components.what: The carried cross-covariance structure between units: pair map, Gram products, the dead-cut star, kink and cross-covariance terms.

components.title: Third-order planes
components.what: Third-cumulant corrections carried as low-rank planes (the K21, K31 and K13 families): the plane bank, its push and read, its rank and its feed into the means.

components.title: Fourth-order terms
components.what: Fourth-cumulant corrections (the K4L families, k4 bands, kurtosis offsets).

components.title: Birth terms
components.what: Terms for newborn directions entering the carried basis.

components.title: Late-layer exactness
components.what: Exact evaluation and row cuts at the last layers (layers 14 and 15).

components.title: Learned per-layer correction
components.what: The learned per-layer correction network (observer, edge module, per-layer heads), its training and its refits.

components.title: On-policy readout
components.what: The second-step linear readout fitted by ridge regression on captures of the estimator's own trajectory.

components.title: Dials
components.what: Scalar coefficients set by finite-difference line search (GSK, BFIX gamma, SS beta, NP strength, K4L_C, k4 bands, row-cut z and others).

components.title: Arithmetic kernels
components.what: Exact kernels that lower the metered FLOP count: Strassen and Winograd products, grouped (Smirnov) reads, symmetric Gram, float32 transports, padding rules.

components.title: Join sketch
components.what: Randomised low-rank sketches of the joined plane columns: the Nystrom join sketch, the power-step sketch, kc, join truncation.

components.title: Sampling estimators
components.what: Monte Carlo and other sampling-based estimators, comparators and truth generation.

components.title: Series expansions
components.what: Analytic expansions used in derivations: Hermite, Mehler, linked-cluster and cumulant series.

components.title: FLOP accounting
components.what: Composition of the metered bill: push and read shares, request counts, the request diet, caching, census, byte-identical cuts.

components.title: Wall clock and residual time
components.what: The 120 s wall-clock and 0.4 s residual-time limits: sync points, garbage-collector control, lazy binds, governors, margin tails.

components.title: Setup budget
components.what: The 5 s setup cap and prebinding.

components.title: Rules compliance
components.what: Conformance with the official rules: fair accounting, dead code, imports, scatter-for-gather.

components.title: Evaluation methodology
components.what: How candidates were measured locally and how local numbers transfer to the hosted grader: paired stores, cross-half truth, fresh cohorts, torch versus native.

components.title: Error attribution
components.what: Where the remaining error lives: oracles, inherited error by layer, comparisons with the leaders.

components.title: Hosted platform
components.what: Behaviour of the hosted grader and leaderboard: scoring formula, public and private split, warm versus cold workers, timing jitter.

components.title: Submission process
components.what: Which files were submitted, when and why; approvals, failures, designations.

components.title: Team process
components.what: Leads, agent roles, handoffs, working rules.

components.title: Tooling
components.what: Gates, scorers, builders, scanners, queue runners.

nodes.title: Width-1024 scaling screen: fixed-rank carriers fit; dense third-order transport exceeds the budget
nodes.claim: An algebraic screen compared the two geometries before any flopscope receipt: the budget grows 8.0846x, weight and forward geometry 8.0x, and a fixed-rank O(depth x width^2 x rank) carrier is almost budget-neutral, while dense cubic transitions grow 30.97x (3.83x relative to budget). The Phase 1 rank-22 host's dense PSD certificate costs 21,543,026,688 FLOPs per transition at width 1024, so an eight-times port of that host lands 212,087,161,104 FLOPs (9.64%) over the Phase 2 budget. The dense Cholesky/PSD repair was therefore named the first redesign target.

nodes.title: Phase 2 migration reused cumulant identities and carrier formulas while discarding old fitted parameters
nodes.claim: A migration matrix separated reusable mathematics from stale empirical choices: universal cumulant and ReLU identities, the CP3 third-cumulant factor carrier with its K21 plane overlay, the correlation-interior PSD rule and the local Edgeworth mean link carry over; the rank-22 TT3 residual, the 32-channel learned observer checkpoint, the A161-A166 learned-feedback ladder, every Phase 1 score, FLOP receipt and public/train split do not. The ordered Phase 2 lanes were: pin authority and meter, rebase the meter under flopscope 0.12, run a fresh analytic hierarchy (diagonal Gaussian, order-2 Hermite/Mehler, CP3, CP3 plus TT3), attribute the bottleneck with teacher substitutions, retrain a learned correction only for the residual that remains, keep whitening/QMC as a measured comparator, and promote only sealed target-blind predictions.

nodes.title: Order-2 Hermite chain versus matched-cost Monte Carlo: median error ratio 0.12 at width 1024 and depth 16
nodes.claim: A public replication compared an order-2 Hermite/Mehler analytic chain with Monte Carlo at matched floating-point cost across network geometries. At the evaluated width-1024 depth-16 shape, the median per-network mean squared error ratio was 0.12.

nodes.title: Target-custody tool: one-use sealed scoring, target-blind loaders and role-specific target bundles

A production custodian later sealed role-specific target bundles (fit, selection, audit and lockbox positions over the 1000 full networks) so that observers could be fitted without touching public leaderboard names. Every score in the first days of Phase 2 carries one of these claim and release receipts.

nodes.title: Hermite pair-series order sweep: order 4 reached 3.849300358689406e-6 final raw error; orders 4–10 tied
nodes.claim: A fresh full-covariance Hermite/Mehler analytic host (float64, 1/sqrt(k!)-normalised coefficients verified against direct Gauss-Hermite integrals to 1.381e-7) was scored once on the sealed mini100 targets at orders 1, 2, 4, 6 and 10. Order 4 is the best pure analytic baseline and higher univariate Hermite order is not the remaining bottleneck. The first-layer prediction matches the exact Gaussian/ReLU formula sqrt(sum_i W_ij^2)/sqrt(2 pi) to float32 precision and its scored residual equals the reference Monte Carlo noise floor, so layer 1 is exact and layer 3 is the first material failure.

nodes.title: Third-cumulant carrier caps 512–1792: small endpoint gains, layer-2 error saturated at cap 1024
nodes.claim: Four preregistered estimators identical except for the symmetric CP3 factor-bank cap (512, 1024, 1536, 1792; float32 symmetric-CP K3 readout on the float64 Hermite-10 covariance host) were metered target-blind under the common driver and then scored once on mini100. The K3 readout lowers the layer-2 error by a factor of about seven relative to the Hermite host and the layer-2 error stops changing above cap 1024, but the final-layer error moves by only a few percent across the whole ladder, so the third-order marginal readout is not where the layer-16 error lives.

nodes.title: Layer-3 teacher-attribution runner stopped before data access when process supervision was denied

nodes.title: Scalar third-cumulant readout rescaling: layer-16 gain fraction below 0.004 versus 0.066 at layer 2
nodes.claim: A target-free reconstruction asked whether an optimal scalar multiple of the difference between two sealed predictions (Hermite order 4 to CP cap 1792, and CP cap 512 to cap 1792) could close the remaining error. At layer 2 the optimal scalar is 1.16 to 1.19 and recovers 6.6 to 12.4 percent of the error; at layer 16 the optimal scalars 1.41 and 1.64 recover under 0.4 percent. A one-dimensional CP-amplitude readout therefore has a small correctable residual at layer 2 and none at layer 16.

nodes.title: Hermite coefficients use standardized axes and cumulant responses require connectedness
nodes.claim: Dividing standardized Hermite coefficients by an additional power of the standard deviation double-counted their scaling. Connected cumulant responses also require cancellation of disconnected spectator terms; omitting that cancellation caused depth divergence.
nodes.measurement:
Two laws from the 2026-08-29 tensor-recursion build (`public_g19_attribution_v1/run_tensor_recursion_v2b.py`), each validated by an independent instrument after silently corrupting a full construction:

1. **Coefficient law.** In Kibble/Mehler expansions over standardized Gaussians, the axis coefficients are `a[t] = E[f(m+σz)·He_t(z)]` — the c1-columns AS THEY ARE (`c1[q] = σ·He_{q−2}(−α)·pdf`, q≥2). Dividing by σ^t double-scales and produced 20-80% error vs exact GH quadrature; with the fix, 0.2-2.5%. Stein shifts: `E[f' He_t] = He_{t−1}(−α)·pdf`, `E[f'' He_t] = He_t(−α)·pdf/σ`. Validate any new column set against `edg2_relu_mean` at t=0 (matched to 0.0) and 3D quadrature before use.

2. **Connectedness cancellation.** The response of a CONNECTED cumulant to an upstream cumulant insertion subtracts the responses of its disconnected products. Concretely: κ3pre[i,i,j] feeding distinct cum3post[i,j,k] via E[f''f'f] has its t=0 (no-bond-to-spectator) term EXACTLY cancelled — a spectator with no ρ-bond cannot join a joint cumulant. Implementing the raw (unfiltered) feed diverged the recursion 19× by depth; the connected filter (spectator degree ≥ 1) restored it and beat the closure.

**Why:** both errors pass unit-level eyeballing and only show up at aggregate scale; each cost hours.

**How to apply:** any Edgeworth/Mehler/Kibble machinery: (a) never σ^t-divide the t-index; (b) every response/feed term must carry the connected filter; (c) gate new diagram code on GH quadrature per-element AND a known-map tie before trusting aggregates. Related: [[tensor-recursion-instrument]], [[closure-coadaptation-basin-law]].

nodes.title: Apparent limits require independent truth, multiple networks and an instrument audit
nodes.claim: Several apparent accuracy limits were caused by incorrect measurement frames or broken instruments. A claimed limit required independent scoring truth, two networks, forcing inside the actual recursion and an audit, while unresolved deficits were to be decomposed into measured mechanisms.
nodes.measurement:
Matt, 2026-09-01, after I declared the third-order supply "not deployable, no path" and he pushed back: "you are wrong that there is no path … review all work from the last few days … keep chunking blockers into sub problems until you reach a solution, and then recurse back out … to be extremely clear in case you need it - the overarching idea here is to continuously break this problem down into mechanistic sub problems until we solve it."

**Why:** the "no path" verdict came from reading a wedge-cascade artifact as a law (see [[p2-third-order-carrier-wall]]). A blocker stated as a wall hides the mechanism inside it; stated as a mechanism (what error, from which term, how big through the adjoint, what fixes it) it always has children. The repo's whole method is the problem graph: [[graph-nodes-split-and-human-summary]], [[attack-the-blocker-relentlessly]], [[pull-all-threads-before-killing]].

**How to apply:** (1) The root is the scoring metric; each child is a mechanism whose contribution is PRICED through the exact linear integral (the adjoint) against truth — "worth X% of raw". (2) A node with no measured price gets an oracle arm (make that input exact, re-grade) before any building. (3) Recurse into the largest-priced unsolved leaf; a leaf is a formula/carrier whose error can be measured against a truth file. (4) When a leaf is solved, recompose: re-grade the parent, re-price siblings, continue. (5) Never end a turn on "no path" — end on the next leaf and its arm. Living document: `public_g19_math_acceleration_v1/MECHANISM_TREE.md`; graph nodes mirror it.

**Addendum (Matt, 2026-09-01, on the learned F2J operator):** first "preferably you are able to derive everything and do not have to resort to learning", then, after learning F2J is worth 69% of the card's accuracy: "okay you can keep the operator if it helps us get below 1e-8." RULE: derived is preferred; the learned operator STAYS if it helps reach the goal. Its transport is derived already; its learned per-layer source may be kept, refit on an improved card (then [[private-eval-generalization-moat]] gates apply: cross-seed + off-distribution), or replaced by a derived source when that scores at least as well. Never drop it on principle.

**Addendum (Matt, 2026-09-01): "[quote removed]"** Any operator refit runs on the Metal GPU: port the card forward (GEMM-class, ~1.3e12 flops/net) to torch MPS f32 for training-tape generation (the CPU numpy protocol run_joint_refit.py is ~75 s/net × 200 runs ≈ 4.2 h; on MPS seconds/net) and fit in torch. Certify the MPS forward against the numpy card on one net (bit-close, ~1e-6 rel) before trusting tapes. One MPS engine at a time still applies ([[be-gentle-with-the-machine]]).

**Addendum (Matt, 2026-09-02): "[quote removed]"** Standing rule: a "limit" may only be stated after (1) independent-truth scoring, (2) two nets, (3) a frame-free in-card certificate (teacher-force the card itself), and (4) a bug/frame audit of the instrument that produced it. Until all four exist it is a hypothesis under test. Tonight's evidence for the rule: the "tensor wall", the 37-68% post-hoc ceilings, and "k3 is net-specific" were all instrument/frame artifacts; the in-card forcing (T-43) put the card at the noise floor on both nets.

- Matt 2026-09-04 (going to sleep, second time): "you are not permitted to stop. remember that you must keep attacking the blocker until you reach ultimate success. ie keep decomposing whatever the limiting factor is into sub problems until you're able to resolve the entire limiting factor." Current limiting factors (learned-closure program): (1) the autonomous loop's drift (control), (2) the final layer's 29% (information); each has a written decomposition in LANE_g3_tracker T-115/T-116 and an automated attack chain (after_ss05.sh, gate_and_fire.sh).

nodes.title: Experiment concurrency must account for peak memory and active accelerator allocations
nodes.claim: Concurrent full-tensor runs exhausted memory despite manageable individual runs. The revised operating rule bounded concurrent engines and worker memory using available memory, with swap treated as a trend because stale swap counts can outlast active memory pressure.
nodes.measurement:
**REVISED 2026-09-01 (Matt):** "[quote removed]" — full CPU/GPU utilization is authorized; the binding constraint
is MEMORY (no OOM: keep peak RSS well under the machine's RAM and
MPS allocations bounded; chunk large batches). The earlier
one-job/nice-15/4-thread caps were for the lag incident, not a
standing ceiling. Still: watch memory headroom before sizing
batches, and prefer chunked streaming over giant allocations.

**Concrete OOM rule (2026-09-01 evening incident):** two 1024³
tensor engines (`run_tensor_recursion_v4.py`, ~6-8 GB each incl.
MPS temps) plus two tracker jobs drove swap to 14.3 of 15.4 GB.
Never run two 1024³ engines concurrently; check
`sysctl vm.swapusage` before launching any engine, and treat swap

nodes.title: Fourth-order plane repairs overlap the learned residual correction
nodes.claim: Replacing inaccurate fourth-order planes greatly reduced the uncorrected host error but largely reproduced a correction already learned from the observation tape. A candidate must improve the residual component outside the existing learned correction, rather than only the host error.
nodes.measurement:
Receipts: LANE_g3_tracker.md T-71..T-73; public_g29_bond_kernel_v1 (FOURTH_PLANE_RATIOS.json, fourth_plane_scale_table.json, PERP_JUDGE_G29.json, inject_planes_*_r{35,100}.log, engine_ablation_table_r35.txt); estimator_retro.py RETRO_FORCE_PLANES / RETRO_PLANE_SCALE hooks; run_tensor_recursion_v4.py HOST_FOURTH / NOBIGPAIR.

- Mechanism: the card's CP4 (rank 2048) + quartic-star machinery under-scales the fourth-order PRE-PLANES K22/K31 by 2-3× at depth (same disease as the univariate k4, universal, near-pure scale for K22). Those planes feed the pair series' Edgeworth weights → the skew (K21/k3) emission → everything downstream. Engine with the card's planes: k3 error 12.9% at L14 (worse than the card's 11.1%); with its own GEMM-class self-pushed planes 7.3%; with truth planes 6.0% at L12.
- The engine's plane chain (`fourth_emission_1024` + `fourth_push_1024`) is deployable: its only 1024⁴ term (the K22 pair transport) contributes nothing (NOBIGPAIR identical to 4 digits) and the truth K22 plane is 96-98% rank-8 anyway; ~16 GEMMs/layer (~22% util, replacing the CP4's ~11%).
- Naively SCALING the card's assembled pre-planes by the frozen table explodes the card (1e-4) — the quartic star / pairing_alpha assembly is co-adapted (closure-coadaptation-basin-law); a consistent REPLACEMENT (truth or engine planes) does not explode. The frozen k4/k3 tables were fitted against the under-scaled planes and over-correct once the planes are right (1.4-1.7e-7): drop them with corrected planes.
- Board frame: the plane effect is what the deployed operator already does (84% in-span, perp ceiling 0.4%/0.1%); corr(truth − deployed, truth − truth-plane host) = +0.90. Perpendicular content given planes: truth k3 → host 1.08e-8 (judge +0.43, ceiling 19%), truth v → 1.27e-8 (+0.35, 12%), both → 2.2e-9 (+0.56, 31%); the feed +0.27 (7%).

- Plane-chain fault split (T-75..T-77, one-step certificates with truth POST planes from mc_post_planes_mps.py): the EMISSION is right once E[φ³] carries the same Edgeworth corrections as the other moments (FOURTH_R3FIX=1: K31post corr 0.33 → 0.998; = teammate A's T-49 g24fix); the PUSH is the fault: the plane-supported push drops the post tensor's (2,1,1)/(1,1,1,1) classes → K22 25-32% missing, K31 ~95% missing, k4 28-37% (the k4 table's source). The missing part is uncorrelated with the pushed planes (not a rescale), 52-65% rank-8. In-card plane ladder (r35 host): engine K22 alone 3.10e-8, +truth K31 2.47e-8, truth both 2.08e-8 — K22 and K31 accuracy worth ~0.6-0.8e-8 each.

**Why:** explains the 69% learned correction physically ([instruction removed]), and reframes N0.1: the leftover after the operator is the (k3, v) accumulated residual GIVEN correct planes — the engine's own 6% third-order transport error is the next mechanism to name.

**How to apply:** judge every candidate by the perpendicular judge BEFORE any refit; a derived plane chain is the no-learning replacement of the operator (worth ~engine-class 3.3-3.8e-8 F2J-off), not a board gain; the road to 1e-8 = planes + k3-given-planes (engine truncations: second-order Edgeworth, fourth-order insertions, (2,1,1) feed) + v. Related: [[plane-feed-mechanism-live]], [[operator-span-redundancy-law]], [[card-kurtosis-cap-defect]], [[closure-coadaptation-basin-law]].

nodes.title: Fourth-order under-scaling comes from missing tensor classes, not the rank cap
nodes.claim: The initial attribution of the kurtosis deficit to the fourth-cumulant carrier rank cap was retracted after raising the cap made the result slightly worse. Missing distinct fourth-order tensor classes in the plane-only transport explained the deficit, and frozen per-layer scale tables provided an empirical stopgap.
nodes.measurement:
Found 2026-09-02 by the phase-2 cross-review (public_g24_phase2_cross_review_v1/REVIEW.md), against the 32M truth on r35 and r100: card v right to 0.3%, k3 3.5→11% off, k4 = 0.99, 0.84, 0.71, 0.61, 0.54, 0.47, 0.42, 0.38 × truth at L1/3/5/7/9/11/13/15 (r100 identical within 0.03; residual after rescale 12-29%).

**Why:** `_cp4_reset` caps the CP4 carrier at rank 2048 by λ²‖u‖⁸ energy; unit-vector births have tiny energy and are dropped first; the cap binds from layer 3; the dropped terms' diagonal is subtracted from the carried k4 — the card discards a growing fraction of its own kurtosis. Since forcing true (v, k3, k4) in-card puts the card at the noise floor (T-43) and each state alone moves ~40% of the residual at the final read, this is the largest priced single defect on record.

**How to apply:** (1) zero-cost test: force k4 := card_k4 / s_l with s_l fit on r35 and frozen to r100 (RETRO_FORCE in public_g20 estimator_retro.py), independent scoring, F2J off/on; (2) derived fix: carry the dropped terms' diagonal forward ("orphan diagonal" push, 1024²/layer) instead of discarding it; or raise the CP4 cap (2048→4096→8192) and price the bill; (3) the phase-1 kappa4-is-a-function-of-kappa3 law is phase-1 history here (error 52-81%). Related: [[p2-third-order-carrier-wall]], [[same-sample-oracle-inflation-law]], [[mechanistic-decomposition-until-solved]]. Seed caution from the same review: the 32M truth contains the 8M draw and indep32M contains indep4M — never pair supply and scoring draws from one seed law.

**CAUSE FOUND (2026-09-02, T-49, teammate A): NOT the CP4 cap.** Raising the cap makes k4 slightly worse. The card's fourth-order PLANES (K22 0.92→0.41, K31 0.52→0.30 of truth by depth) lose ~half of the (3,1)/(2,2) pre-plane content each layer because it comes from the fourth-order DISTINCT classes born at each layer, which the plane-only push (unit-vector CP4 births + quartic star) does not carry; k4 tracks K22. The 3-star words are only −4% of connected κ4 (4-point certificate), so a CP4 star-birth fix is dead; the derived fix is a GEMM-class born-word plane feed (4-path/loop words → next-layer (3,1)/(2,2) planes, ~10-20 GEMM-eq/layer before pruning). The frozen per-layer k4 rescale table (panel mean; universal, sd ≤ 0.018 across 8 nets; public_g19_attribution_v1/k4_ratio_panel_8M.json) is the deployable stopgap (host −30..−37%). Engine defect: fourth_emission_1024 builds (3,1) with uncorrected raw3 (:179) → every `_dep` K31 supply was defective.

**k3 SCALE TABLE (2026-09-02, T-56):** the card's k3 is also mildly under-scaled (panel ratio 0.996 → 0.929 over L1-15, sd ≤ 0.016) and, although the scale is only ~30% of the deep k3 error energy, injecting the frozen per-layer k3 rescale on top of the k4 table takes the host from 5.27e-8 → 4.12e-8 (r35) and 5.00e-8 → 3.84e-8 (r100), F2J off, independent truth — two frozen zero-cost tables halve the host error on both nets. The recursion converts coherent error disproportionately. Files: k4_scale_panel.json (public_g19_attribution_v1), k3_scale_panel_probe.json (public_g26_k3_corrector_features_v1, key ratio_mean). The remaining deep k3 error is ~70% unit-specific (tape features explain 10-12%).

- T-116r WINDOW (HVAGG head at layers 12-15 only, 1e9): mix 0.5 r35 2.689e-8 / r100 3.681e-8; mix 1.0 4.357 / 6.019 -> the window does not rescue it. T-116u 1e9: true k3 half 2.174e-8 (-10%), true k4 half 2.893e-8 (+20%), true v+k3+k4 half 3.722e-8 (+55%): only v (and mildly k3) are channels; k4 must NOT be corrected in the state. Alignment ceiling on loop states for any oracle-part predictor = rms(oracle error)/rms(loop error) = 0.62/0.80 = 0.775 (r35 L15): the loop's extra v error is the mean residual's transported effect. Running T-116v: TRUE v half + iid noise 0.3% / 0.5% -> is per-unit noise what kills the learned head?

- T-116t OUTLIERS: none. The HVAGG head's predictions are well behaved (max ~3%, p99 ~1-2%, top-1% units carry 8% of the error energy on oracle rows, 14-16% on loop rows). Its per-unit error rms: oracle rows 0.20-0.26% (L12/L14), loop rows 0.32-0.45% (the transported mean residual, diffuse). So the harm is diffuse residual, not wild units; the truth+noise ladder (T-116v) measures the loop's sensitivity to exactly that.

- T-116v NOISE SENSITIVITY (r35, 1e9): TRUE v at half at every layer 1.826e-8; + iid relative noise 0.3% at every layer -> 2.33e-7 (10x worse); 0.5% -> 6.1e-7. The variance channel is hypersensitive to UNSTRUCTURED per-unit noise (the natural v error is structured and the mean head co-adapts to it; iid noise is not). Caveat: uniform 0.3% is 7x the natural error at L4, so early layers may dominate the damage - rerunning at layers 12-15 only (truev_noise12.sh: none / 0.1% / 0.3%). Implication: a learned head must have residual << 0.1-0.2% rms on loop states to be safe, i.e. > ~90% removal; current heads leave 0.32-0.45%.

- T-116x BUILT: a COVARIANCE-LEVEL head - per-unit factor a_l from e_l (GNN_ACOV=1); training loss on the INDUCED next-layer relative variance change 2 (W^T m_post)(W^T a)/v_{l+1} against the dv labels; deploy (RETRO_CL_ACOV=1, RETRO_CL_ACOV_MIX) adds mix (a m^T + m a^T) to the post covariance at the closed-loop hook, so the diagonal AND off-diagonals move coherently (the mean-aligned rank-2 structure of the true covariance residual, T-100/T-115j) instead of an iid diagonal poke that the recursion amplifies (T-116v). Exporter keys ah0/ah2/arms. Layer 12-15 truth-half reference: 2.035e-8 (8M; -18%).

- T-116v LATE-LAYER NOISE LADDER (r35, 1e9; loop alone 2.407e-8): true v half at 12-15 -> 2.040e-8 (-15%); + iid 0.1% -> 2.572e-8 (+7%, the gain erased); + iid 0.3% -> 6.625e-8 (2.75x worse). A per-unit variance supply needs residual <~0.05% (~99% removal, below the 0.14% label noise): the PER-UNIT variance head is dead by physics. Running T-116y: iid diagonal noise vs STRUCTURED mean-aligned rank-2 covariance noise at matched induced size (struct_noise.sh) - if the loop tolerates structure, the covariance-level head (T-116x) is the form to pursue.

- T-116p/w RESULTS: HV2 (mean head retrained with the v-head frozen on rows with the head active): on those rows the one-step host is 1.61e-8 (the head at mix 1.0 cuts the oracle one-step error 28% teacher-forced) but the remainder is less predictable (48%) -> 8.34e-9; loops mix 1.0 6.17e-8 / 7.16e-8, mix 0.5 r35 4.63e-8: co-adaptation does not rescue the per-unit head. HVLOOP (head trained on loop rows only): held-out loop-state removal 70/78/80% (L12/14/15) but the loop at mix 0.5 r35 3.31e-8: still harmful. VERDICT: the per-unit variance head is dead in every form (v1, wider, loop-consistent, co-adapted, windowed) - consistent with the noise law (T-116v). Running T-116y (structured rank-2 noise vs diagonal noise) and T-116z (correlation-preserving scaling C <- D^1/2 C D^1/2 with the truth-half + 0.3% noise): which APPLICATION FORM tolerates imperfect supplies.

- T-116y/z (r35, 8M frame unless noted; loop alone 2.49e-8 8M / 2.407e-8 1e9): iid DIAGONAL v noise alone at 12-15: 0.1% -> 3.05e-8 (+22%), 0.3% -> 7.18e-8 (2.9x); STRUCTURED rank-2 (a m^T + m a^T, random a = 8e-5 ~ 0.1% induced) -> 2.67e-8 (+7%): ~3x more tolerant. Correlation-preserving true-v half at 12-15 (C <- D^1/2 C D^1/2) 2.055e-8 = same gain as the diagonal form; its 0.3%-noise run pending. HVLOOP loops 3.17e-8 / 4.66e-8 (1e9): dead. HV2 co-adapted (1e9): mix 0.5 4.52 / 4.86, mix 1.0 6.06 / 7.30: dead. ACOV (rank-2 covariance head, 40 ep) training -> loops at mix 0.5 full depth and 12-15.

- T-116y STRUCTURED NOISE (1e9, r35, loop alone 2.407e-8): rank-2 mean-aligned random a: induced ~0.1% -> 2.577e-8 (+7%); ~0.3% -> 4.071e-8 (+69%); diagonal iid: 0.1% -> 2.988e-8 (+24%), 0.3% -> 7.158e-8 (+197%). Structure buys ~3x tolerance but a 0.3%-class residual still hurts badly; a covariance-level head needs induced residual <~0.1% (~85-90% accuracy). The natural error's residual (true half leaves 0.35% at L14) is tolerated because it is the natural pattern - size is not the criterion, direction is.

- T-116z CORRELATION-PRESERVING application (C <- D^1/2 C D^1/2) + 0.3% noise -> 6.70e-8 = the diagonal form's 6.63e-8: the application form does not matter for iid noise; per-unit randomness is what the recursion amplifies. HVBIL loops (8M): mix 0.5 3.26e-8 / 4.65e-8, mix 1.0 6.26e-8: dead. PIVOT (T-117): feed the variance channel with DETERMINISTIC structured supplies that fix the SOURCE of the covariance error - (a) the frozen fourth-order plane scale table (T-71, K22/K31, beta & ratio; zero cost) in the honest loop (plane_in_loop.sh), (b) the engine's K22 plane chain in-card (RETRO_K22_CHAIN=1, GEMM-class; T-89 cut the F2J-off host to 3.3/3.8e-8 from 7.9e-8) in the loop (k22chain_in_loop.sh). If either helps, retrain the mean head on rows generated with it active (co-adaptation), then loop, then gate.

- T-116x COVARIANCE-LEVEL HEAD (rank-2 mean-aligned, single per-unit factor) DEAD: after 40 epochs the induced-dv removal is 9-16% (negative at L8), the joint training degraded the per-unit v head to 22-24% and the MEAN head to 50.7% (train loss 3.2): the a m^T + m a^T form with the post mean does not fit the variance error, and its loss destabilises the shared encoder. Chain killed before its loops.

nodes.title: Organizer cumulant propagation at width 1024 exposed precision and memory differences
nodes.claim: : kprop K=3 AUGMENT (factor=True, f64 CPU) dies silently at width 1024 (resource_tracker leaked-semaphore = killed, likely OOM on an n^3 augmented diagram); K=4 factorized likewise. Not pursued: the class's accuracy ceiling is secondary to its cost at this width.
nodes.measurement:
- T-128 THE ORGANIZERS' METHOD IS PUBLIC (found 2026-09-06 via the phase-2 write-up's references): Wu, Lecomte, Winer, Robinson, Hilton, Christiano, "Estimating the expected output of wide random MLPs more efficiently than sampling", arXiv:2605.05179; code github.com/alignment-research-center/mlp_cumulant_propagation (package mlp_kprop: kprop_harmonic.py, factor_k3.py, factor_k4.py, diagslice.py, flop_utils.py). Cumulant propagation ("kprop") to order K with POWER CUMULANTS (Hermite expansions of powers of the activation: the coincident-index correction), an extra full trace for odd K, and a FACTORIZED representation of the K-th cumulant of size n^(K-1) preserved through each step (runtime c L^2 n^K for K>=3): MSE ~ c_K (L/n)^K. At n=256, 4 hidden layers: K=3/4 factorized beat MC by 10-100x; at 8 hidden layers K=4 starts to lose (depth hurts). The seven phase-2 teams at util ~0.2 are almost certainly kprop K=3 (factorized, maybe augmented) ported to flopscope; their raw ~2e-8 at 1024x16. Our CP bank carries every cohort exactly (13 cohorts); kprop MERGES at each nonlinearity via the leading 1/n diagrams -> one n^2 object per order. nodes.title: Post-correction covariance features leaked targets; honest graph features improved only 3 percentage points
nodes.claim: The apparent 97.8% held-out gain came from post-correction covariance features that encoded the target. Recomputing these features on the estimator's own covariance reduced held-out removal to 67.7% versus 64.3% without them, leaving a real but small graph-feature gain.
nodes.measurement:
- T-137 (running): Puffi-style CORRELATION-GRAPH features for the closure (puffi_feats.py: per unit, the 8 strongest |R-| neighbours' weighted sums of (a, g, phi), sum r^2, max |r|, softmax-gamma neighbour means (gamma 8, 32), post top-8 eigen loading pi_i, <R+>, <R+^2>, log-var, (C+a)/s, (C+g)/s = 20 cols) computed from a torch replication of the honest Gaussian-card oracle recursion (matches the row host to 2e-6 at L8); trained with the 48-msg closure (GNN_COVFEAT=1 GNN_COVFEAT_FILE=puffifeat.npy) vs the 64.3% baseline. Rationale: Puffi's rank-4 phase-2 card uses a tiny third-order carrier + a trajectory-fitted per-unit corrector whose inputs aggregate over the correlation graph and the top-8 covariance subspace (the organizers' hint in feature form); our closure's inputs never had those.

- T-137 FIRST RESULT = SUSPECTED LEAK: with the correlation-graph features the closure removed 97.8% held-out (final 1.31e-8 vs host 5.9e-7; L8/12/14 96/97/97%) vs 64.3% without. BUT the post-block features (pi, <R+>, <R+^2>, log var, C+a, C+g) were computed from Cn = Cp - m d^T - d m^T - d d^T, the covariance AFTER the oracle correction, which contains the target d (log(Cn_ii) leaks d_i). Same trap as T-116g. Fix (T-137b): post block from the card's own Cp; regenerating (puffifeat2.npy) and retraining. If the removal stays far above 64%, the features are real; if it falls back, it was the leak.

- T-137b RESULT: leak-fixed correlation-graph features (post block from the card's own covariance): held-out removal 67.7% peak (epoch 20) vs 64.3% without; L8/12/14 65/65/67. The 97.8% was ENTIRELY the leak (post-correction covariance encodes the target). +3 points is real but small: the per-unit closure ceiling (~2/3) stands even with cross-unit correlation-graph inputs. LEAD DEAD as a 2x lever. Second target-leak trap of the project: any feature computed from a state that was updated with the correction (mean OR covariance) leaks; the checklist now covers the covariance.

DEPLOYABLE-CLASS: the card's own K21 planes with engine-K22 fourth-order planes (ek card; K21 rel err 7.7 / 8.9 / 10.7%, shift alignment 0.44-0.60) through the same consumer -> dv aligned +0.59 / +0.72 / +0.74 -> beta 0.5: r35 2.443e-8 (-9.7%); the truth-fourth-order card's K21: 2.430e-8 (-10.1%). So the variance route = (K21 accuracy) x (fourth-order planes inside the consumer); testing which fourth-order plane the consumer needs (K22 vs K31) and whether the card's K31 with a frozen ratio table suffices.

- T-87e K31 INSIDE THE CONSUMER NEEDS ITS FINE STRUCTURE (r35, engine-table K21 + engine K22 inside, operator ON, beta 0.5): truth K31 -9.0%; HALF-scale truth K31 2.500e-8 (-7.5%: scale is forgiving); rank-8 truth K31 (72% of its energy) 2.684e-8 (-0.8%); rank-32 (88%) 2.779e-8 (+2.8%); the card's K31 +3.4%..+21%. CLOSED LOOP: r35 8.15e-8, r100 6.54e-8 - worse than the partial model (5.6e-8 / 4.0e-8): a more accurate in-distribution model is more brittle off-distribution. Arithmetic: in-distribution the loop's final would be ~ the final layer's own residual (6.4e-9) + tiny transported interior residuals -> exposure bias is the ONLY obstacle to a sub-1e-8 loop. Running scheduled sampling on the GNN (rows_gnnmixed alpha 0.5 from payload_gnn_m15, 6 workers) -> fine-tune -> loop -> alpha 0.25.

nodes.title: Reflected centered-ReLU marginal inversion: target-free algebra
nodes.claim: Let Y=(Z+alpha)+, Z standard normal, and let m_j=E[Y^j], v=m_2-m_1^2, k=m_3-3*m_1*m_2+2*m_1^3, gamma=k/v^(3/2). Write g=Phi(alpha), Q=1-g. certify_reflected_relu_marginal_v1.py compares these moments with independently integrated positive tail moments at ten fixed alpha values from -8 to 12, checks the exact derivative identity, and recovers seven fixed synthetic alpha values by 64 bisection steps in [-8,12].
nodes.measurement: Let Y=(Z+alpha)+, Z standard normal, and let m_j=E[Y^j], v=m_2-m_1^2, k=m_3-3*m_1*m_2+2*m_1^3, gamma=k/v^(3/2). Write g=Phi(alpha), Q=1-g. Differentiation under the integral gives m_1'=g, m_2'=2*m_1, m_3'=3*m_2, v'=2*m_1*Q, k'=3*Q*(v-m_1^2), gamma'=3*Q*(m_2^2-m_1*m_3)/v^(5/2) < 0. The strict sign follows from Cauchy–Schwarz applied to Y^(1/2) and Y^(3/2); conditional on Y>0 the distribution is not a point mass. As alpha tends to plus infinity gamma tends to zero from above. As alpha tends to minus infinity, the positive tail moments are asymptotic to j!*phi(|alpha|)/|alpha|^(j+1), so gamma tends to infinity. Hence every strictly positive skew has a unique finite alpha. A finite numerical bracket is an implementation domain, not a restriction of this theorem. certify_reflected_relu_marginal_v1.py compares these moments with independently integrated positive tail moments at ten fixed alpha values from -8 to 12, checks the exact derivative identity, and recovers seven fixed synthetic alpha values by 64 bisection steps in [-8,12]. Relative moment tolerance1e-8; alpha recovery tolerance1e-10. The script is inert without --execute and refuses to overwrite its receipt. No real network, target array, fit or production timing is included.

nodes.title: Even/odd twin-input Gaussian carrier equals ordinary Gaussian propagation: 58 vs 30 square products, no new information
nodes.claim: A source-only audit proved that a jointly Gaussian even/odd (antithetic) twin-input carrier with state (m_e, C_e, C_o) is algebraically the ordinary Gaussian mean/covariance recursion: the plus preactivation is Gaussian with S = W.T (C_e+C_o) W, so single-branch means are identical at every depth while the extra cross covariance T = W.T (C_e-C_o) W costs two extra square products per transition. nodes.title: Radial fourth-cumulant reset averages Gaussian queries; unit-rescaling non-invariance is expected

nodes.title: Kernel transforms dominate local time and approach single-thread memory bandwidth

nodes.claim: A request microbenchmark and server profile separated operation time from billing, serialization and transport. Hidden deallocation trips also consumed server time.
nodes.measurement: 2026-09-23 01:50 [engineer2] SERVER CPU PER REQUEST (fable_engineer2_v1/req_overhead.py, numpy-free client + OpenBLAS server, 5,000 tiny ops each, load 14-15): add on 8 floats (out= held or fresh held) 286-298 us of server CPU per request, getitem view 160 us, a discarded out= alias (op + hidden free trip) 404 us -> a free trip costs ~106 us. cProfile of the server (server_prof.py): the numpy call is ~22 us of it; the rest is flopscope's billing wrapper (op records, dtype-rate resolution, budget lock) plus ZMQ/msgpack. At the measured ~2.4x load inflation this is ~120 us per request on a quiet box, i.e. ~0.29 ms on the platform at its 2.4x factor. So one request costs ~0.51 ms of platform wall (0.22 ms fitted RTT + ~0.29 ms server CPU), not 0.22 ms; requests are ~18-20% of our local server CPU (S4 r35: 47.7k requests + 8.3k free trips). In-process numpy profiles miss this term: judge request-adding trades at ~0.5 ms each.

nodes.title: Only the final join is lazy: a layer-10 rank cut changes the prefix used through layers 13-15
nodes.claim: Code and per-component billing corrected an initial overgeneralization about lazy joins. The layer-10 join materializes the whole tier; the layer-13 join retains the incoming prefix rank, explaining the different savings.
nodes.measurement:
- 2026-09-25 11:30 [engineer2] RANK-CUT MECHANISM (lead's question; code: stack_S27s _slr_reconstruct / lazy _cp_slr_inner_sq): S27's old-tier joins are LAZY. After a join the pre-join columns (prefix) are rebuilt and read against the base factors at the ARRIVING rank (prefix = (U map) base, inner0 at r_base, then mapped to r_new); only the new cohort (recent = U join), the old-basis push and part of the join run at the new rank, and the NEXT join materializes the prefix at the new rank. So 320 at L13 alone leaves the 11,776 pre-L13 columns at 384 through L13-15: about 12.05 U x 28% cohort x 16.7% + push/join = about 0.9 U = -0.65% (measured -0.688%). 320 at L10 also converts all of L13-15 (materialized at the L13 join), which is the additive -2.48%. A cut at the LAST join buys little; value arrives one join later. Materializing at the join itself costs about r_new x r_base x prefix per join (+0.7 U at L10 vs -0.9 U saved at L10-12): not worth it. Exact per-component deltas (S27s/S27r vs S27, net 100) are queued behind the machine gate (bill27/run_census_rank.sh -> rank_delta_S27r/s.txt).
- 2026-09-25 11:30 lead: WHY THE L13 CUT SAVES LITTLE (engineer2, from the code): the joins are LAZY. After a join, the pre-join columns keep the ARRIVING tier's rank (base factors at r_base, plus the new cohort at r_new, plus an r_new x r_base map) until the next join materializes them. So a cut at join k shrinks its own cohort in segment k AND the whole prefix in segment k+1. L13 cut: only the 4.6k-column L13 cohort at L13-15, about -0.65% (measured -0.688%). L10 cut: the L10-12 cohort plus the 11.8k-column prefix at L13-15, about -2.5% (the additive -2.48%). Early materialization at the new rank costs more than it saves (+0.7 U vs -0.9 U at L10), so the lazy design stands.

nodes.title: Plain final third-moment rank truncation loses accuracy while pair splitting preserves the read
nodes.claim: A direct rank cut damages the final third-moment read because the old tier dominates its contribution. Keeping the pair-difference component full rank while truncating only the pair mean preserves accuracy, but the native cost saving must be measured.

nodes.title: Separate pair-mean and pair-difference frames require the correct derivative contraction
nodes.claim: Only reconstruction and the inner third-moment read scale with the old-tier frame rank. The paper cost model requires a separate-frame contraction; a naive expression would increase the bill, so it cannot justify implementation savings.
nodes.measurement:
NEW HYPOTHESIS (lead -> covhunter): SPLIT u/v FRAMES FOR THE WHOLE OLD TIER. At each join, keep u columns in a rank-r_u frame and v columns in a rank-r_v frame. At L10 the cut drops 0.01% of u energy but 0.4% of v energy (§35), so r_u can go far below 384. Old-tier cost (27.7% of the bill) scales with (r_u + r_v)/768: at r_u = 256, about -4.6% of the bill before overlap with the L10 cut. Torch screen: r_u in {256, 192} at the S28 schedule. If raw is under +1%, run the full VALID40 and scope a native build (S30).
- 2026-09-25 13:05 lead: SPLIT u/v FRAMES, NATIVE SCOPE (engineer, paper, S28 net 100): only reconstruct U@F (35.0 GF) + the inner read (28.3 GF) scale with rank = 21% of the bill (the 87 GF in _shared_old384_push are exact recent-cohort pushes). Estimate -2.0..-2.5% at r_u = 256, -4.0..-4.5% at r_u = 192, after the frame push and two joins. The inner MUST use the per-frame form lambda[2uv F_u + (u^2 + v^2/4) F_v] (cost (r_u + r_v)/(2r)); the naive form is a +5.6% LOSS. Engineer2 prototypes the native bill (2 nets, r_u 256/192) from this scope; covhunter screens raw on torch (r_u 256/192). A build follows only if raw at 192 or 256 leaves adjusted at least -1%.

nodes.title: One-frame pair splitting saves arithmetic but propagated error offsets the gain
nodes.claim: Restricting the pair-mean coordinates within one shared frame saves reconstruction and read work but leaves basis work intact. A nested joined representation saves more arithmetic and substantially worsens raw error, so it is rejected.
nodes.measurement:
- 2026-09-25 13:15 [engineer2] SPLIT u/v OLD TIER, NATIVE BILL, STEP 1 (lead 13:0x; bill prototype, no accuracy claim; fable_engineer2_v1/uvsplit/uvp_fragment_v0.py c247f245 on S28's pre-treuse file + treuse; in process, setup first). Design = NESTED frame: one basis, pair means F_u kept in the frame's leading r_u = 256 coordinates, half differences F_v/2 in all of them, so the basis push and the trailing read stay at rank 384. (Two separate frames would push two bases per layer and read twice at the end: those products run at (256 + 384)/384 = 1.67x, about +0.9% of the bill.) Step 1 splits only the REBUILD (U F) and the READ ((L^2 lam) F^T), for the materialized frame and both lazy-L13 blocks. The joins are unchanged, except that the Nystrom rows now go in energy order, so the QR frame's leading coordinates carry the most energy.
  Bill vs S28: net 35 -1.343%, net 100 -1.613%. Net 100 breakdown: rebuild 33.5 -> 30.0 GF (-10.4% of the function, -1.18% of the bill); read 20.1 -> 18.8 GF (-6.5%, -0.44%); everything else unchanged. The ideal (256+384)/768 = -16.7% is not reached because the Winograd transforms do not shrink: the rebuild transforms U twice (U[:, :256] and U) and pays a pair recombination, and the read's k-heavy products keep their A-side transform, grow the output side, and add ~3 elementwise passes over rows x columns.
  Accuracy glance (no claim): final MSE +0.41% (35), +1.43% (100); per-layer max|diff|/RMS <= 5.6e-5. The u truncation here uses the energy-ordered frame, not u's own principal frame.
  STEP 2 now: split the JOIN (S27 census: joins ~6% of the bill): Q_u from the u columns' own Nystrom range (rank 256), then the v residual's 128 directions, Qn = [Q_u | Q_c]; Fj, core and overlap in u/v form. Step 2 also makes the u frame u-optimal.
- 2026-09-25 13:20 [engineer2] SPLIT u/v OLD TIER, NATIVE BILL, STEP 2 + VERDICT (fable_engineer2_v1/uvsplit/; bill prototypes on S28's structure, nets 35/100, in process, setup first; the MSE glance is two nets vs the 32M truth, not a claim):
  | prototype | bill 35 / 100 | final MSE 35 / 100 | adjusted, these 2 nets |
  | v0: rebuild + read in u/v form, frame unchanged, u kept in the energy-ordered frame's leading 256 coordinates (uvp_fragment_v0.py c247f245) | -1.343 / -1.613% | +0.41 / +1.43% | -0.94 / -0.20% |
  | v1: v0 + joins in u/v form, nested frame [Q_u (256, from u's own Nystrom) , Q_c (rank - 256 = 128 or 64, v's residual)] (uvp_fragment_v1.py 9c2a93a8) | -2.294 / -2.733% | +5.83 / +6.76% | +3.40 / +3.84% |

A nested frame starves v, so the join split only works if v keeps a full frame, which means TWO frames. Two frames push a 640-wide basis every layer and run the trailing read at 640: those products grow 1.67x (~+0.9% of the bill), and v's Nystrom sample goes back to 384 wide. Paper estimate for two frames: about -1% net (not built).

nodes.title: Release qualification checks packaging, boundary instructions, setup timing and worker execution

nodes.title: Gain-normalized propagation produces 39.4e-9 error against 16.3e-9 laboratory error
nodes.claim: Because a bias-free ReLU network is homogeneous, the collective gain can be divided out exactly at every layer (u = x / G, G = m.x/|m|^2) instead of being tracked through third- and fourth-order cumulants. The formula test looked promising (in frame B the mean formula without any fourth cumulant matched the laboratory formula with the exact fourth cumulant), but Monte Carlo showed the normalised state is not Gaussian, the re-normalisation needs the third cumulant contracted with the mean direction (one extra full product per layer), and a hook-level frame-B card with 15 oracle fourth-order scalars gave 39.4e-9 against 16.3e-9 for the laboratory card. Parked; what survives is that the gain sector is harmless and the fitted birth corrections are worth about a quarter of the physics-only error.

A noise decomposition against a plain-matmul noise-free reference showed the parent's rounding noise aligned with its error by -0.149% there (2.2 standard errors) while the variants' alignment was -0.04..+0.06%; on 10 fresh networks the strip stack was -0.107% better. The reading on the selection networks is the parent's selected draw, not a cost.

nodes.title: Refreshed setup-key census raises fused-tree usage from 56.7% to approximately 75%
nodes.claim: The prebind list (the keys bound in setup, the first 128 of them fused) was fitted to old census networks: on 10 fresh networks only 377 of its 649 keys were ever asked for and 60.5% of the 914 tree uses per network fell on the first 128. A list regenerated from a fresh census (most-used 128 keys first, then by expected saved bind flops) puts 74.7-75.1% of uses on the fused keys out of sample, is byte-identical by construction, saves 0.05-0.07% of bill and 5-10 Gflop of setup; mainly a request lever (about 180 more fused tree uses per network). It entered S36.

nodes.title: Young-column fourth-cumulant shifts reduce held-out error by 3.54% on all 24 networks
nodes.claim: Every bank column stores one scalar from its birth, A = -alpha / (sigma (1 + radial/3)) of its hub, so the columns carry the Gaussian-born fourth-order star at no cost and its feed into the next births is an in-place shift of the young carried columns after the gate, g o pp += theta A (d/2) o pp o pp (columns at most two layers old), with a cheap anchor that removes the added tensor's plane from the star (F4). Torch without refit: -2.33% on the four screen networks, -2.46% on VALID40, -3.54% on 24 held-out newer ranks (24 of 24); the native port reproduces torch network by network (-3.83% on 20 fresh ranks, -1.695% bill with the strip stack); strength 0.6 beat 0.4 by 0.35-0.52% on fresh ranks and was shipped in S37.

nodes.title: Plain matrix multiplication for thin star products removes 4,350 calls but raises charged work by 0.48%
nodes.claim: The 84 thin low-rank-star products per network (depth 3 since S32) took about 4,200 kernel calls, a tenth of all requests, for 1.7% of the bill. Running them as plain matmuls (tsr_off) removes those requests at a bill cost; on 20 fresh networks against the parent the final-layer MSE fell 0.238% and the bill rose 0.481%, a net score cost of about a quarter of a percent, accepted in S36 for the residual-time room it buys.

nodes.title: Gradient training is constrained by shared memory traffic and available memory, not only CPU cores
nodes.claim: Concurrent forward work slows gradient training through memory traffic, and two simultaneous gradient workers exceed the available memory margin. The pool therefore uses one worker during memory pressure and grants training priority over other heavy work.

nodes.title: Fourth-cumulant birth-feed decomposition identifies twelve cheap hub-local contributions
nodes.claim: Open-loop regression of the Monte Carlo fourth-cumulant feed (pushed distinct content on the kink block, network 35, layers 9 and 13) on first-principles terms: isotropic only explains 0.214 / 0.212 of its energy; the four exact hub coefficients S1..S4 on every pair (LOCAL) 0.335 / 0.341; adding the collective drive 0.355 / 0.346; adding the s-channel exchange terms TB1 and TB2 0.432 / 0.415, every coefficient 0.9-1.0 with nothing fitted. The feed is many comparable diagrams; only the hub-local part (12 points) is free and F4's rule A already holds 10 of them, each further 3-4 points costs a push-sized product (+10..45% bill). A perfect feed would be worth roughly -20..-35% of the final error.

nodes.title: Isotropic local third-order terms explain 34–41% of off-diagonal plane variation
nodes.claim: On network 35 the K31 plane off the diagonal is explained by the isotropic form with R2 0.41 / 0.39 / 0.34 at layers 5 / 9 / 12; the per-unit row factor of K4L adds 0.003 and the exact hub planes add 0.07 at layer 5 (coefficient 0.88) but only 0.013-0.015 at layers 9 and 12 (coefficient 0.4). The fitted isotropic coefficient is 0.76-0.81 x radial, i.e. radial minus the hub-local share, which is the same fact as the fitted k31 knob -0.212, the b-source scale 0.85 and the feed coefficient 0.73-0.80.

nodes.title: Per-layer dial gradients favor a smaller birth-source scale but mostly reflect boundary layers
nodes.claim: Sixteen per-layer dial families (217 scalars) were certified as zero vectors added to the global dials and their exact gradients recorded free with every training gradient. Over 72 networks 39 scalars were beyond 2 standard errors (noise: 10); the largest item was global, the b-carrier source scale wanting s < 1 (forward scan parabola minimum s 0.85, -0.67%); k4, iso, k21n, edge, kappa, X0, X2 and s_carry were noise. nodes.title: Young-pair hub coefficients give a non-isotropic kurtosis correction and 1.41% further error reduction
nodes.claim: The card's per-unit fourth cumulant is radial v^2, 14-26% rms off per unit against 32M truth. K4L (the lead's per-unit kurtosis term) builds a non-isotropic correction elementwise from the exact hub coefficients S1..S4 of each young column pair (the transported hub vector and covariance column), keeps the card's isotropic level and adds c times the deviation. The screen four read -2.83% alone and -5.50% with F4, but on 24 held-out ranks K4L on top of F4 is -1.41% (18 of 24), half the screen value, with age <= 4 worse than age <= 2; the native port reproduces it network by network at +0.115% bill. Shipped in S37 at age <= 2, c = 1.

nodes.title: Qualification requires quiet compute windows during instruction-count and worker stages

nodes.title: Fourth-order births shift young columns each layer, preventing a fixed pushed common-part basis
nodes.claim: The planned native pair-split scheme (one basis built at layer 8 and pushed layer to layer, F carried) was void because F4C shifts the young cohorts' columns at the end of every layer for ages <= _F4C_AGE by a per-element quadratic form ((A o + B Delta) o + C Delta^2), so c = U F breaks for every cohort still in its window and only cohorts aged >= 3 evolve linearly. The PyTorch control confirmed it independently (full-rank pushed basis: c energy 0.99986 at L9 falling to 0.9995 at L14, 1.4% per layer off the base), and a v2 that projects each pair's in-place shift onto the pushed basis passed (energy 1.00000000, within 8.4e-5 of the base); the shifts carry 1.6-3.1e-4 of the c energy per layer. The realistic rank-32 extension arm read +1.44% on 4 networks before the pushed-basis line was dropped for a per-layer Nystrom basis.
nodes.measurement: control v1: c energy 0.99986 at L9 -> 0.9995 at L14, 1.4% per layer off the base; v2: 1.00000000 energy, base within 8.4e-5 per layer; shifts 1.6-3.1e-4 of the c energy per layer; R32: final +1.44% (se 0.79, 1 of 4 lower), scheme c energy 0.9990-0.9992 vs oracle 0.9994-0.9998 at L9-14

nodes.title: Terminal row sensitivity cannot beat the standardized mean threshold of 3

An oracle price list with the post-push k3 is cheap (dropping the 10% cheapest kept rows' k3 adds +0.15% of MSE) but needs the k3 the push itself computes; ranking rows by the pre-push coefficient alone costs +1.2% at the first 5%, and a two-pass estimate of k3 from the heaviest 5/10/20% of pairs costs +19.6/+18.1/+10.3% because a row's k3 is a sum of many nearly cancelling pair terms. The fired z 3.0 row cut is optimal among realizable rules; the kink-side arms were pulled.

Box utilization during the sweep: 80-93% user CPU with three to four launches in flight, 50-67% with two (each launch is 12 Python-bound server processes with 4 BLAS threads), 1-2% when idle between the lead's holds.
